$comment: Saldo's queryable task graph (ADR 0019). A dependency-aware DAG so 'what is the highest-value READY task' is computable, not buried in prose. Validated + queried by tools/backlog.mjs (pnpm backlog). Edit by hand; keep it honest. status: todo|in_progress|done|cancelled. value: high|medium|low. effort: S|M|L. depends_on: ids that must be done|cancelled first. cancelled tasks carry cancelled_reason (and optionally superseded_by).

tasks.title: EU AI Act readiness & compliance
tasks.notes: DONE (ADR 0022): source-grounded against Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (eur-lex CELEX 32024R1689 + AI Act Explorer; raw captures in db/reference/eu-ai-act/). Only the LLM features are AI systems (Art 3(1)/Recital 12); NOT prohibited (Art 5), NOT high-risk (Art 6/Annex III); provider+deployer, not a GPAI provider (relies on Art 53 docs). Binding duties: transparency (Art 50, 2 Aug 2026) + AI literacy (Art 4, in force). Delivered the cited knowledge page, ADR 0022, the .claude/rules/ai-act.md gate + AGENTS.md invariant. Forward product/repo work = the aia-* tasks.

tasks.title: Receipt/invoice -> structured proposal via vision-LLM (propose-only)
tasks.notes: The first AI-system surface (spec 8.5 / Phase 4; ADR 0009 local-first). image -> extraction -> Zod -> rules engine -> proposed voucher -> human confirms. AI never writes the ledger (ADR 0002). Carries the EU AI Act obligations (aia-*).

tasks.title: EU AI Act: disclose AI interaction in the UI (Art 50(1))
tasks.notes: Tell the user, at first interaction, that a value/proposal is AI-generated (unless obvious). Applies by 2 Aug 2026. See eu-ai-act.md s4.

tasks.title: EU AI Act: AI-output provenance + 'AI-assisted' label + logging (Art 50(2))
tasks.notes: Every AI-proposed value carries machine-readable provenance (model+version+confidence) in its Zod contract, is labelled AI-assisted, and is logged (pino). This is where the code-level provenance gate lands (a required field + a lint/test check).

tasks.title: EU AI Act: capture the upstream GPAI model's Annex XII docs (Art 53)
tasks.notes: At the LLM-hosting decision (Phase 4): capture the chosen model's capabilities/limitations docs under db/reference/llm/ — rely on the provider's documentation, never infer from memory.

tasks.title: EU AI Act: proportionate AI-literacy note (Art 4, in force)
tasks.notes: A short dated competence note: what the AI features do, their limits, the propose-only/confirm model. Art 4 in force since 2 Feb 2025; proportionate for a solo/small team.

tasks.title: EU AI Act: conformity self-assessment checklist
tasks.notes: A dated checklist re-run before each AI feature ships and at each Art 113 milestone: prohibitions clear (Art 5), still not high-risk (Art 6/Annex III), transparency met (Art 50).

tasks.title: EU AI Act: high-risk guard — never score/profile a natural person
tasks.notes: DONE: AGENTS.md invariant + .claude/rules/ai-act.md (auto-loads on AI/LLM code). No feature may evaluate a natural person's creditworthiness or profile them (Annex III 5(b); Art 6(3)) without re-opening ADR 0022.

tasks.title: EU AI Act: fold the AI Act review into privacy-reviewer when AI code lands
tasks.notes: When the AI surface exists, extend the existing privacy-reviewer subagent with the AI Act checklist (transparency, provenance, no high-risk scoring) + wire the aia-provenance-logging code gate; split out a dedicated reviewer only on demonstrated need (ADR 0022).
